correctness.rationale: The bright/dark orthogonal split reduces unperturbed absorbing dynamics to a stable three-site bright block plus the zero generator on the two classwise sum-zero dark spaces. The unperturbed zero Liouvillian eigenvalue is semisimple; Hilbert–Schmidt dissipativity proves strict stability at any positive site dephasing. The projected noise generator is self-adjoint negative definite and sends each classwise dark projector to minus its class rate divided by its class cardinality. A finite-dimensional Schur complement gives the stated all-density-matrix \(\varepsilon^{-1}\) coefficient with bounded remainder. Exact rational projection checks (648) and 240 independent numerical projected-dynamics and small-rate comparisons validate selected boundary cases but do not substitute for the analytical proof.

value.rationale: The coupled two-orbit complete bipartite network is a natural exactly specified quantum trapping model, and the singular integrated survival time is an intrinsic physically motivated absorption invariant. The formula determines a graph-size and partition-dependent noise clock, identifies the coherent bright-versus-dark boundedness dichotomy for every initial state, and separates two independently tunable dephasing mechanisms. The result goes beyond a computational census or a routine reparameterization of the previously handled one-sided star graph.
